challenges.content:
Site name: Parcelwise Help
Support link: Contact support
Heading: Frequently asked questions
Intro: Quick answers about shipping, billing and your Parcelwise account.
Categories (label: Categories): Getting started, Billing, Shipping and labels, Account and security, Integrations
Current category: Billing
Category heading: Billing
Category intro: Eight questions about plans, invoices and payments.
Questions and answers:
Q: When will I be charged?
A: Your card is charged on the same day each month as the day you upgraded. Label postage is charged separately, at the moment you buy each label.
Q: Can I switch between monthly and yearly billing?
A: Yes. Switch in Settings, then Billing. Moving to yearly takes effect at once and credits any unused days of your monthly plan.
Q: Where do I find my invoices?
A: Every invoice is listed under Settings, then Billing, then Invoice history, and a PDF copy is emailed to your billing contact on the day it is issued.
Q: Which payment methods do you accept?
A: Visa, Mastercard and American Express, plus ACH bank transfer on yearly plans.
Q: Do you offer refunds?
A: Yearly plans can be refunded in full within 30 days of purchase.
Q: How do I add a tax ID to my invoices?
A: Enter it under Settings, then Billing, then Company details.
Q: What happens if a payment fails?
A: We retry three times over seven days and email you before each attempt.
Q: Can I cancel at any time?
A: Yes. Your plan stays active until the end of the current billing period.

challenges.content:
Agency: Stackwell
Site links: Services, Case studies, About, Contact
Page label: Case study · Retail (part of Case studies)
Heading: How Greenleaf Grocers cut checkout drop-off by 38%
Intro: A regional grocery chain was losing one in two online baskets at checkout. In twelve weeks we rebuilt the flow around speed and fewer decisions.
Headline results (figure: meaning):
- 38%: fewer abandoned checkouts
- 2.4x: faster checkout page loads
- $1.2M: added yearly online revenue
The challenge: Greenleaf runs 46 stores across Oregon and Washington. Online orders had doubled since 2024, but almost half of the shoppers who reached checkout left before paying. The checkout asked for an account, five pages of details and a delivery slot chosen last.
What we changed: We cut checkout to a single page, made guest checkout the default and moved the delivery slot to the start, so shoppers knew their time before they filled in anything else. Page weight fell from 3.1 MB to 1.2 MB.
Client quote: "For the first time, our online checkout feels as quick as our fastest till."
Quote by: Dana Whitfield, Head of Digital, Greenleaf Grocers
The results: The new checkout launched on 1 April 2026. Completion rose in the first month and kept climbing as returning shoppers got used to it.

Jan 52% (old checkout), Feb 54% (old), Mar 53% (old), Apr 61% (new), May 68% (new), Jun 71% (new)
